chapter: Life on the road and in the Webb band's book
title: Building a new band for Louis Armstrong under Joe Glaser
summary: Glaser sent McRae to hear Armstrong's old band in Roanoke; later McRae replaced a drinking brass section.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: So, this is the same thing what we do with bands. I did it with, (inaudible), when I did it with Cab.
I did the same thing when I did it with Louie Armstrong. With Louie, I built Louie a complete new band. That was a different type of thing.
Joe Glaser wanted to get rid of the old band. He didn't want nobody in the old band, because he said the band wore its use out.
He say, "Well, I'll build Louie Armstrong a new band. I want you to build me a new band."
He says, "Louie is playing down in Roanokes. I want you to go down and take a listen to

the band," you know. And I took a trip down there and got down there about 10:30. I went over to the ballroom while they was playing. (inaudible).
I was standing in the back of the band and the whole band was playing, and Louie was going like mad, and nobody was getting any hands.
I found out -- I say, "These guys are -- Jesus, the band do need changing."
Because Louie was blowing and nobody was giving -- and the place was packed -- and his had wasn't -- wasn't getting that. Nothing, you know.
Jumping forward here,
(inaudible) Louie Armstrong's band had a lot of changes in the trumpet section.
Yeah.
Well, we kept changing them. I changed the whole section of trumpets when I was in California when I told you fellows (inaudible) got to drinking.

I changed the whole --
I called Benny Carter up. He was playing downtown at the theater -- the Paramount Theater.
I say, "Look" -- he say, "You can have my whole brass section. I'm breaking up the band. I'm going to stay out here and write."
And I took like (inaudible), Fats Sleepy I used to call him. Fats Gordon -- I picked a couple of other trombone players.
Change the whole (inaudible) brass section.

Wasn't no -- shipped the boys back home. (inaudible), Pull the band off the air because you couldn't depend on the brass. They were blue notes making (inaudible) and things like that. You couldn't have that on a coast-to-coast (inaudible) broadcast. Joe Glaser come, "What's wrong with that brass?"
I say, "They drinking."
I say, "Take the band off the air"
Cut out the last two broadcasts, (inaudible). I say, "I want to change the whole brass (inaudible)."
We changed them, let the guys go, Paid their car fare and sent them home and brought in the
